A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same relaxed rotation-equivariant convolution, backbone and detector research, with SBDet renamed R2Det. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection and classification results, equivariance ablations, convergence analyses and feature visualizations in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 reports original detection, classification and instance-segmentation results, together with additional controls, perturbation analyses and robustness examples.

M1.justification: The central filter-perturbation procedure, separable convolutions, backbone and detection neck remain. Algorithm 1 generalizes C4 to configurable Cn and replaces Gaussian perturbation initialization with uniform initialization; coordinate mapping changes from nearest-integer rounding to flooring. Appendix 7.6 adds an adaptation using a segmentation head. These are extensions and refinements of the retained design.

E1.justification: v2 adds instance segmentation on COCO-seg, extending evaluation to mask prediction, and a stretched-object detection scenario in Figure 6. VOC, COCO detection, CIFAR-10/100 and the custom rotated-MNIST task remain; the latter is relocated and renamed, rather than newly introduced.

E2.justification: COCO comparisons add YOLOv9/v10, Gold YOLO, YOLOMS and GELAN variants in Tables 6 and 16. Segmentation introduces YOLOv8-seg and RTMDet-Ins comparators. Conversely, the VOC comparison drops SSD, R-FCN and other older detectors present in v1 Table 3, and CIFAR comparisons remove Res2NeXt-29.

E3.justification: v2 introduces C2/C8 configurations, an expanded classification size/group grid, zero-initialization and noisy-filter controls, COCO AP75 and size-specific AP, and box/mask segmentation metrics. VOC ablations previously labelled validation results are now labelled test results, without establishing whether experiments were rerun. The detector convergence comparison also switches from AP50:95 in v1 Figure 8 to AP50 in v2 Figure 4.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands tests of why relaxation helps: strict-versus-relaxed comparisons across group orders and both detection datasets, a naive learnable-noise control, zero-initialization sensitivity, learned-perturbation diagnostics and a stretched-object case study. The initialization study changes from Gaussian variance to uniform bounds, while the original detection-loss plots disappear. Rotated-MNIST robustness and CAM analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates for performance. The means and variances added in v2 Table 12 describe learned perturbation values, rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Many results are added or removed, including segmentation, group-order controls and the removal of the class-wise VOC breakdown. The medium detector's reported COCO AP50:95/AP50 changes from 52.7/69.6 to 53.1/70.3. R2Net-M CIFAR-10 accuracy changes from 96.5% after converting v1's error rate to 97.3%. These are revised reported results under changed method/settings, not established same-setting gains; the rotated-MNIST error values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Definition 2 replaces the norm-bounded definition of relaxed equivariance with a coset-based definition; the former returns as approximate equivariance in Appendix 7.10. That appendix adds strict/relaxed convolution proofs, and the parameter analysis generalizes to Cn. Proposition A.3 is substantively revised as Proposition 7.3, bounding the model's equivariance residual rather than the difference between two equivariance-error norms.

C1.justification: The central convolution, backbone and detector contributions remain. v2 explicitly emphasizes rotational symmetry breaking, advertises Cn/Rn with 4n additional parameters, and broadens the introduction's novelty claim from object detection to vision tasks. Its conclusion restricts the state-of-the-art claim to detection, whereas v1 jointly claimed detection and classification superiority.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking learned perturbations, the noise control and the stretching example to rotational symmetry breaking, and distinguishes zero-initialized relaxed filters from strict ones. However, v1's explicit slow-training and high-memory limitations in Appendix A.9 and its CUDA-related future direction are removed, rather than relocated.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-address disclosure and systematic detector/classifier hyperparameter tables covering optimizers, learning-rate schedules, momentum, regularization, warm-up, loss weights and augmentation. It also specifies initialization and head implementation details. These substantially improve documentation; newly disclosed training budgets do not establish changes to previously reported experiments.

R1.justification: The positioning relative to strict and relaxed equivariant networks remains central. v2 adds Curie's-principle and symmetry references, including Chalmers, Earman and Gross, and updates detector coverage with YOLOv9/v10. It removes the earlier GNN background and EON/TED discussions, producing a more focused research context.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten, filter construction and convolution exposition are separated, and experimental and appendix sections are reorganized. Renaming SBDet to R2Det accompanies widespread terminology changes, a new title and revised author/header material. These changes extend well beyond accommodating additional experiments.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the opening schematic, consolidates and redraws architecture diagrams, redesigns the equivariance visualization, and adds the stretching figure and several differently structured tables. Convergence plots are reorganized into the main text, while loss plots and the class-wise VOC table disappear. Retained feature-map and CAM displays are relocated; these are substantial visual changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added group-order and noise controls test the proposed mechanism more directly, while the hyperparameter tables substantially improve reproducibility documentation. These benefits are tempered by removal of the explicit training-speed/memory limitations and new reporting inconsistencies: Figure 6 shows strict-model confidence falling from 0.94 to 0.88, while its discussion claims an 11% decrease. The expanded evidence therefore supports a limited net quality improvement.
